objective: Add one registry-wide conformance gate that validates every registered scenario against the shared safety, provenance, replay, evidence-freshness and release-status guarantees, requires a committed failure corpus per scenario identity, and reports per-scenario results so CI names the scenario and the failed rule.
decision_supported: Whether a newly registered scenario can enter the registry without proving it honours the shared fail-closed boundaries, and whether an existing scenario can silently drop one.
acceptance: the gate discovers every manifest under sim/registry without a hand-maintained allow-list, because adding a manifest must add it to the gate matrix
a registered scenario with no committed conformance case set fails the gate, and a case set missing a required dimension fails, so a new scenario without required tests fails CI

the committed corpus declares a case for stale evidence, conflicting evidence, missing provenance, replay determinism, an unsafe/raw-control field and release-status truthfulness for every registered identity
each declared case names a test file and a test function that exist, so a case cannot be satisfied by prose

derived probes independently confirm the manifest declares no raw control or e-stop authority, that a fixture is never release eligible, and that replaying one event stream twice yields an identical state hash
the gate emits machine-readable per-scenario results and a human summary that names the scenario identity and the failed rule, and uses 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 INCOMPLETE
the gate is read-only: it imports no simulator, writes no run or event, and never starts ROS, Gazebo or hardware
evidence: pytest transcript for tests/unit/test_scenario_conformance.py with the passed count
check_scenario_conformance.py stdout showing five registered identities, their dimension coverage and exit code 0
a failing run showing a scenario that lacks a case set is reported by identity and by rule
ruff check and ruff format output
make scenario-check and make context-check output
stop_conditions: the change would require editing a frozen fixture, a seed or a committed matrix document
the change would require editing docs/architecture/scenario-contract-v1.json, which is a reviewed contract amendment
the change would require adding a runtime dependency or importing ROS, Gazebo, MoveIt or a hardware SDK
the change would require a physical or Gazebo claim, which this repository cannot make from a fixture
a scenario would have to be declared conformant without a committed test that proves it
data_classification: public repository source, documentation and test fixtures; no secrets, personal data, credentials or physical measurement data
model_policy: AI may write the conformance rules, the gate, the corpus and the tests; a named human Owner accepts the required dimension set and any scenario added to the registry
risks_and_fallbacks: the gate could become a hand-maintained allow-list; fallback is that the corpus is keyed by registry identity and the gate derives the identity set from the registry every run, so an unlisted scenario is a failure rather than a skip
a scenario could declare a case that does not exist; fallback is that the gate resolves the named file and test function and fails when either is absent

the gate could re-implement the verifiers and drift from them; fallback is that the verifier-semantics dimensions are proven by committed tests the gate only resolves and names, while the cheap invariants are derived from the loaded registry

the required dimension set could block a legitimate scenario; fallback is that a dimension may be declared `not_applicable` with a written justification, and the gate reports it as a notice rather than silently accepting it
rollback is a revert of this commit; the gate is additive, no manifest or fixture changes, and no CI job becomes required until the workflow edit lands
